description: We are RPS Group 3, participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Lusaka, Zambia. Our challenge is “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.” We are passionate about space exploration, coding, and technology. Our goal is to create an interactive guide exploring how humans could survive on Mars. We welcome creative, enthusiastic members interested in programming, design, research, science, and problem-solving. Together, we aim to turn ideas into innovation!

details:
ARES is a web-based mission-control tool designed for Mars exploration, featuring an interactive map that allows users to navigate Mars terrain, inspect geological and elevation data, and plan routes while avoiding hazards using precise pathfinding. The application provides various mission-related information, such as resources, weather, emergencies, and crew status, helping users understand the interconnections between terrain and mission logistics.

Developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, it utilizes the Leaflet library for map functionalities and pulls imagery and data from sources like NASA Mars Trek and USGS, requiring only a standard web browser and internet access. While the project aims to educate, simulate and demonstrate Mars mission planning, it is intended for real-life rover guidance and acknowledges the approximate nature of its terrain data and hazard assessments. Overall, ARES combines a Mars exploration map with mission-control features to enhance understanding of space missions.
